rest.warehouse.answers.unreadableBody: Any endpoint except `GET /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks/queue` and `GET /api/v1/warehouse/merchants/me`, after the token and the caller have been checked, when the body is sent as `application/json` but is not valid JSON. Nothing was applied: correct the body and send it again. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`.
rest.warehouse.answers.badRequestJson: Any endpoint, before the token is checked, when the query string, a path segment or a form-encoded body cannot be decoded: a broken `%` escape, or bytes that are not UTF-8. Nothing was applied. Rails answers with this JSON when `Accept` asks for `application/json` without also listing `*/*`, or when the path ends in `.json`.
rest.warehouse.answers.badRequestHtml: The same failure, when `Accept` is missing, is `*/*`, or lists `*/*` among other types, as browsers, `fetch` and most HTTP libraries send it: the body is Rails' static HTML error page.
rest.warehouse.answers.noToken: Any endpoint, when the `Authorization` header is missing or is not `Bearer` followed by a token. Sign in with identity and send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
rest.warehouse.answers.invalidToken: Any endpoint, when the bearer token is not a valid identity access token for Kinetix: not signed with `RS256` by one of identity's published keys, expired, issued for another issuer or audience, a refresh token or another kind of token, or missing its `sub`, `email` or `role` claim. When the access token has expired, refresh the token pair and send the request again with the new access token.
rest.warehouse.answers.notASeller: Any seller endpoint (every path under `/api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks`, `/api/v1/warehouse/returns` and `/api/v1/warehouse/merchants`), when the token's role is not `seller`. Identity is not asked. An account approved as a seller after it signed in gets a seller's token when it refreshes its session: refresh, then send the request again.
rest.warehouse.answers.notAMerchant: Any seller endpoint, when the token's role is `seller` but identity knows no merchant for the account. Sending the request again does not help until identity knows the merchant.
rest.warehouse.answers.notStaff: `GET` and `POST` on `/api/v1/warehouse/bins`, `/api/v1/warehouse/stock_receipts` and `/api/v1/warehouse/stock_adjustments`, and `GET /api/v1/warehouse/bins/stock`, when the token's role is not `admin`. Checked before any query parameter or body is read.
rest.warehouse.answers.noRouteJson: Any path under `/api/v1/warehouse` that names no endpoint, or names one with a method it does not take (for example `DELETE /api/v1/warehouse/merchants/{id}`): Rails answers `404`, never `405`, before the token is checked. This JSON comes when `Accept` asks for `application/json` without also listing `*/*`, or when the path ends in `.json`.
rest.warehouse.answers.noRouteHtml: The same request, when `Accept` is missing, is `*/*`, or lists `*/*` among other types: the body is Rails' static HTML 404 page.
rest.warehouse.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that the warehouse did not expect; a database it cannot reach is answered `503` `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` instead. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`. A stock receipt or adjustment may be sent again with the same `idempotency_key`; for any other change, read the current state before retrying, because whether it took effect is not known.
rest.warehouse.answers.unsupportedMethod: Any path, when the method is none of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS` and `TRACE`. The warehouse's web server, Puma, answers before Rails sees the request, with an empty body.
rest.warehouse.answers.signingKeys: Any endpoint, when the token names a signing key the warehouse does not hold and its last attempt to fetch identity's published keys failed. The token was not judged and nothing was applied; send the request again after `Retry-After` seconds.
rest.warehouse.answers.identityUnavailab: Any seller endpoint, and `POST /api/v1/warehouse/stock_receipts` unless it replays an earlier receipt, when identity cannot be asked about the merchant: it is unreachable, answers with an error, or does not answer within 5 seconds. Nothing was applied; send the request again after `Retry-After` seconds.
rest.warehouse.answers.databaseUnavailab: Any endpoint, when the warehouse cannot reach its database: the connection is refused or lost, no connection comes free in time, or the database is shutting down, starting up or takes no more connections. The token and the caller's role are checked first, and for a seller identity's answer about the merchant too, so their answers come before this one. Whether a change was written is not known, because the connection can be lost after a commit: after `Retry-After` seconds, send a stock receipt or adjustment again with the same `idempotency_key`, and read the current state before repeating any other change. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`.
rest.warehouse.taskQueue.summary: Lists the seller's work left: tasks still to pack (`received`, `packing`) and packed parcels whose label has not been printed yet, earliest cutoff first. Cancelled tasks and printed parcels are not on it; find those by order number with `GET /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks`. Tasks are not created through this API: order creates one when a buyer's checkout is paid.
rest.warehouse.taskQueue.who: A seller: a token whose role is `seller`, for an account identity knows as a merchant. Identity is asked on every request. A merchant identity no longer lets trade still sees its queue, so parcels buyers have paid for still ship. Only the caller's own tasks are listed.
rest.warehouse.taskQueue.case.listed: The queue, possibly empty. `sla_urgency` is `packed` for a packed parcel; for a task still to pack it is `overdue` once `same_day_cutoff_at` has passed, `due_soon` within 2 hours of it, and `due_today` before that. `tracking_number` is the courier's AWB once one has been assigned, else `null`. Each line says whether a scan has matched it yet (`scanned`); `bin_location` is the bin the order's stock was reserved from, empty when no reservation names one. Keep `id`: the task calls take it.
rest.warehouse.findTask.summary: Finds the seller's own fulfillment task for one order number, in any state: on the queue, packed and printed, or cancelled. A task leaves the queue once its label is printed, so this is how a seller gets the task `id` that opening a return takes.
rest.warehouse.findTask.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade; only the caller's own tasks are found.
rest.warehouse.findTask.field.orderNumbe: The order number as order wrote it (`ORD-…`), sent once as a plain value. Spaces around it are removed; the rest is compared exactly, case included.
rest.warehouse.findTask.case.found: A list holding the one task the caller's merchant has for that order. Beside the queue's fields it carries `updated_at`, the time of the task's last status change, and `label_print_count`, `0` until the label is first printed; it has no `sla_urgency`. `tracking_number` is `null` until a courier is assigned. Keep `id` to open a return.
rest.warehouse.findTask.case.none: The caller's merchant has no task for that order number: another merchant's order, an order not paid yet, or a number typed with different capitals. The answer is an empty list, never `404`.
rest.warehouse.findTask.case.noOrderNumb: `order_number` is missing, blank, holds a NUL character, or is sent as a list or a map (`order_number[]=…`). This is checked after the caller, before any task is looked up.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.summary: Moves one of the seller's fulfillment tasks one step forward: `received` → `packing` → `packed`. A task is `packed` only once a scan has matched every line, with `POST /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks/{id}/verify_scan`. Reaching `packed` tells order the parcel is ready, and order books a courier; setting `packed` again re-sends that report.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade; only for a task of its own merchant.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.field.id: The task's `id`, from the queue or from `GET /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks`, written in digits; leading zeros are ignored. A task of another merchant is answered as not found.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.field.statu: The state to move to, a string: `packing` from `received`, `packed` from `packing` once every line has been scanned, or `packed` again from `packed`. `received` and `cancelled` are states no move leads to, and a `cancelled` task cannot be moved at all.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.moved: The task moved to `packing`. `order_notified` is `false` and `notify_error` and `dispatch_ref` are `null`: order is told only when a task reaches `packed`. `updated_at` is when the warehouse answered.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.packed: The task is `packed` and order accepted the report. `dispatch_ref` is the fleet's reference for the courier booking, empty while order is still booking one. Print the label once the queue shows a `tracking_number` for the task.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.orderU: The task is `packed`, but order was not told: it could not be reached, did not answer within 5 seconds, or failed while handling the report. `notify_error` carries this fixed text. The task stays packed: send `packed` again to re-send the report. Order keeps one courier booking per order, so re-sending a report it did receive books no second courier.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.orderR: The task is `packed`, but order refused the report and `notify_error` is order's reason, for example an order cancelled in the meantime. Sending `packed` again gets the same refusal while the order stays as it is.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.notFou: The caller's merchant has no task with this `id`.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.unread: The `id` in the path is not a whole number from 1 written in ASCII digits, for example `12abc`, `+12` or `1e3`. It names no task, so the answer is the one for an unknown task, and nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.notASt: `status` is sent as another JSON type than a string (a number, `true`, a list, an object) or holds a NUL character. The message names the field: `status must be a string` or `status must not contain a NUL character`.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.missin: `status` is missing, `null`, empty, or only spaces, tabs or line breaks. This is checked before the task is looked up, so nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.unknow: `status` is none of `received`, `packing`, `packed` and `cancelled`, compared exactly; the message starts with the value as it was sent. This is checked before the task is looked up, so nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.notAll: The move is not allowed from the task's current state: a step skipped or taken backwards, or any move to or from `cancelled`. Read the queue for the task's current state.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.unscan: The move is `packing` → `packed`, but a scan has not matched every line yet; the message says how many lines are left. Nothing changed. Scan the remaining lines: the scan that matches the last one packs the task and tells order.
rest.warehouse.setTaskStatus.case.change: Another request moved the task between this request's read and its write, and nothing was changed. Read the task's state again before deciding whether to retry.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.summary: Records a print of the parcel's shipping label and answers its tracking number (AWB) and how often it has been printed. The label exists once order has booked a courier for the packed parcel.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade; only for a task of its own merchant.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.field.id: The task's `id`, from the queue or from `GET /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks`, written in digits; leading zeros are ignored. A task of another merchant is answered as not found.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.case.printed: The print is counted. `id` is the label's own id. `print_count` counts every print including this one, `reprint_count` the prints after the first. A packed task leaves the queue once its label has been printed.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.case.notFound: The caller's merchant has no task with this `id`.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.case.unreadabl: The `id` in the path is not a whole number from 1 written in ASCII digits, for example `12abc`, `+12` or `1e3`. It names no task, so the answer is the one for an unknown task, and no print was counted.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.case.cancelled: Order cancelled the task, after releasing its stock and refunding the buyer, so the parcel is not shipped.
rest.warehouse.printLabel.case.noCourier: No courier has been assigned yet, so there is no tracking number to print. Try again once the queue shows a `tracking_number` for the task.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.summary: Checks a scanned barcode against one of the seller's tasks. A SKU marks its line as scanned; the first match moves a `received` task to `packing`, and the scan after which no line is left unscanned packs it and tells order, exactly as setting `packed` does. A scan of a `packed` task changes nothing and reports nothing: set `packed` again to re-send a report.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade; only for a task of its own merchant.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.field.id: The task's `id`, from the queue, written in digits; leading zeros are ignored. A task of another merchant is answered as not found.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.field.scannedC: The scanned text, a string of at most 128 characters, counted with any spaces around it; those spaces are then ignored. It is compared, regardless of case, with the task's SKUs first, then its order number, then its tracking number. One matching scan marks a whole line, whatever its quantity; when two lines share a SKU, an unscanned one is marked first.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.matchedLi: The code matched a line's SKU, and that line is now scanned. `matched` says what matched (`sku`, `order_number` or `tracking_number`) and `matched_code` is the task's own spelling of it; `matched_sku` is the SKU, `null` when anything else matched. `lines_remaining` counts the lines not scanned yet, and `new_status` is where the task is now: a `received` task moves to `packing` on its first match. `order_notified`, `notify_error` and `dispatch_ref` stay `false`, `null` and `null` until the scan that packs the parcel.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.alreadySc: The SKU matched a line an earlier scan had already marked (`line_already_scanned` is `true`), so nothing was counted twice. A repeated scan is safe: the task moves only as far as the lines left allow, as with any scan.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.paperwork: The code matched the task's order number, which marks no line: `matched` is `order_number` and `matched_sku` is `null`. On a `received` task this starts packing; it never packs a parcel. The tracking number matches the same way, as `tracking_number`.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.packedByS: This scan matched the last unscanned line, so the task is `packed` and order was told, exactly as when the status is set: `order_notified` is `true` and `dispatch_ref` is the fleet's reference for the courier booking, empty while order is still booking one. When two scans race, only the request that moved the task to `packed` tells order. Print the label once the queue shows a `tracking_number`.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.packedNot: The scan packed the task, but order was not told: it could not be reached, did not answer within 5 seconds or failed, and `notify_error` carries this fixed text, or it refused, and `notify_error` is order's reason. The task stays `packed`. Scanning again does not re-send the report; set the status to `packed` with `PATCH /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks/{id}/status`.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.alreadyPa: The task was already `packed`, here matched by its tracking number: nothing changed and order was not told again. A SKU or order-number scan of a packed task answers the same way.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.notFound: The caller's merchant has no task with this `id`; the message names the id sent.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.unreadabl: The `id` in the path is not a whole number from 1 written in ASCII digits, for example `12abc`, `+12` or `1e3`. It names no task; this message names no id, and nothing was scanned.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.notAStrin: `scanned_code` is sent as another JSON type than a string, or holds a NUL character: `scanned_code must be a string` or `scanned_code must not contain a NUL character`.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.codeTooLo: `scanned_code` is longer than 128 characters, spaces around it included. This is checked after the path `id` and the type check, before the task is read; nothing was scanned.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.blank: `scanned_code` is missing or blank. This is checked before the task is looked up.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.mismatch: The code matches no SKU on the task, nor its order number or tracking number; the message lists the SKUs expected. Nothing moved and no line was marked.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.cancelled: The code matched, but order cancelled the task, so there is nothing left to scan.
rest.warehouse.verifyScan.case.changed: Another request moved the task between this scan's read and its write, to a state this scan's step does not lead to, and the step was not taken. A line this scan matched stays marked. Read the task again before scanning again.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.summary: Asks order to open a return for the order behind one of the seller's tasks. Order opens one only for a delivered order whose return window is still open, and at most one per order.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade; only for a task of its own merchant.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.field.fulfillm: The task's `id`, written in digits: from the queue, or from `GET /api/v1/warehouse/fulfillment_tasks` once the task has left it. A task of another merchant is answered as not found.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.field.reason: Why the goods are coming back: a string that is not blank, of at most 500 characters. Spaces of any script count as blank, and a character outside Unicode's Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, counts as two characters, the way order counts them. Order keeps the reason whole.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.alreadyOp: A return was already open for this order. Its `return_number` is answered and nothing new was opened.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.opened: Order opened the return. Keep `return_number`: the goods are reported with it when they arrive, at `POST /api/v1/warehouse/returns/{return_number}/received`.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.notFound: The caller's merchant has no task with this `id`, or the `id` is not a whole number from 1 written in digits.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderNotF: Order answered the call with a not-found status: it has no record of what the request names. Nothing was opened, and the same request gets the same answer. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses an unknown order with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED`.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderConf: Order answered the call with a status saying its records are in a state that does not allow the request. Nothing was opened; read the order's state before trying again. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED` and a reason.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.notAStrin: `reason` is sent as another JSON type than a string, or holds a NUL character: `reason must be a string` or `reason must not contain a NUL character`. Order was not asked.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.blankReas: `reason` is missing, `null`, empty, or only whitespace, Unicode spaces such as U+00A0 or U+3000 included. Order was not asked.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.reasonToo: `reason` is longer than 500 characters, where a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as most emoji, counts as two. Order was not asked; shorten the reason and send it again.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderInva: Order answered the call with a status saying a value in it is invalid. Nothing was opened, and sending the same request again unchanged gets the same answer. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED` and a reason.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.refused: Order answered and refused, and `message` is order's reason: the order is not delivered, its return window has closed and the merchant has been paid, or it is not this merchant's. Nothing was opened, and the same request gets the same answer. The status is `502` although order did answer.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderFail: Order failed while handling the call: an unexpected error in order, order refusing the warehouse itself as a caller, or an answer the warehouse cannot use, such as one holding a NUL character. It is never about the seller's own permissions. Whether order opened the return is not known. Sending the same request again is safe: order opens at most one return per order, and answers `already_open` with its `return_number` if it had opened one.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderUnav: Order could not take the call: it could not be reached, or answered that it cannot serve now, for example because its database is down. Send the same request again after `Retry-After` seconds. In the rare case that the connection broke after order had opened the return, the repeat answers `already_open` with its `return_number`.
rest.warehouse.openReturn.case.orderTime: Order did not answer within 5 seconds, so whether it opened the return is not known. Send the same request again after `Retry-After` seconds: order opens at most one return per order, and answers `already_open` with its `return_number` if it had opened one.
rest.warehouse.receiveReturnedGoods.summ: Reports the goods of an open return as back in the warehouse. Order records them, works out the buyer's refund for what came back, and starts the refund. The goods are not added to the warehouse's stock: staff book what is fit to sell again with a stock receipt.
rest.warehouse.receiveReturnedGoods.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade. Whether the return is this merchant's is checked by order.
rest.warehouse.receiveReturnedGoods.fiel: The `return_number` that opening the return answered, sent exactly as answered: `RMA-`, eight digits, `-`, then eight characters from `0`–`9` and `A`–`F`. Any other spelling, lower case included, names no return.

Optional: the bin the goods were put in, a string that is not blank, of at most 64 characters. Leave it out or send `null` when no bin is named; order then records the return without one. Order records it with the return; it is not checked against the warehouse's bins, and no stock is booked into it.
The goods that came back: a list of at least one object. A SKU may appear on several lines; their quantities add up.
A SKU the order bought: a string that is not blank (Unicode spaces count as blank), of at most 128 characters, with no NUL character.
A JSON integer, or a string of digits, from 1 to `2147483647`. All lines of one SKU together may not exceed the units the order bought.
rest.warehouse.receiveReturnedGoods.case: Goods had already been recorded for this return, and nothing changed. A request sent again after a timeout lands here.
`lines` is present but is not a list of objects.

`return_number` is not written the way order writes return numbers, as in `RMA-20261022-4C7D2E9A`: lower case, spaces, a NUL character or any other length are answered this way. Order was not asked and nothing was recorded. This is checked right after the caller, before the body. A number in the right form that order does not know is refused by order with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED`.

Order answered the call with a not-found status: it has no record of what the request names. Nothing was recorded, and the same request gets the same answer. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses an unknown return number with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED`.

Order answered the call with a status saying its records are in a state that does not allow the request. Nothing was recorded; check the return before trying again. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED` and a reason.
`bin_code` is sent as a JSON number, `true` or `false`, a list or an object, or holds a NUL character: `bin_code must be a string` or `bin_code must not contain a NUL character`. Order was not told.
`bin_code` is an empty string or only whitespace, Unicode spaces included. Send a bin's code, or leave the field out. Order was not told.
`bin_code` is longer than 64 characters. Order was not told.

The lines break a rule, and the message names the first one broken, in this order: `Name at least one SKU that came back` when `lines` is missing or empty, `Every line needs a SKU, written as a string` for a SKU that is missing, blank, not a string or holds a NUL character, `Every line's SKU must be at most 128 characters` for a longer SKU, and the message shown for any other quantity, a fraction or `true` included. Order was not told.

Order answered the call with a status saying a value in it is invalid. Nothing was recorded, and sending the same request again unchanged gets the same answer. Order's current release does not answer this call this way; it refuses with `RETURN_NOT_RECORDED` and a reason.

Order answered and refused, and `message` is order's reason: no return has this number, it is another merchant's, it was rejected, or a line names a SKU or more units than the order bought. Nothing was recorded. The status is `502` although order did answer.

Order failed while handling the call: an unexpected error in order, order refusing the warehouse itself as a caller, or an answer the warehouse cannot use, such as one holding a NUL character. It is never about the seller's own permissions. Whether order recorded the goods is not known. Sending the same request again is safe: order records a return's goods once, and answers `already_recorded: true` if it had recorded them.

Order could not take the call: it could not be reached, or answered that it cannot serve now, for example because its database is down. Send the same request again after `Retry-After` seconds. In the rare case that the connection broke after order had recorded the goods, the repeat answers `already_recorded: true`.

Order did not answer within 5 seconds, so whether it recorded the goods is not known. Send the same request again after `Retry-After` seconds: order records a return's goods once, and answers `already_recorded: true` if it had recorded them.
rest.warehouse.merchantMe.summary: Answers the caller's merchant record in the warehouse: its `id`, which `PATCH /api/v1/warehouse/merchants/{id}` takes, its packing cutoff hour, and whether identity lets it trade. The record is created by the first request of a merchant identity knows.
rest.warehouse.merchantMe.who: A seller whose merchant identity knows, including one identity no longer lets trade.
rest.warehouse.merchantMe.case.found: `principal_id` is the merchant's identity principal. `cutoff_hour` is the hour on the platform's clock up to which a new task is due the same day; a new merchant starts at `12`. `may_sell` is identity's answer at this moment.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.summary: Sets the merchant's same-day packing cutoff hour. A task created up to that hour on the platform's clock is due the same day, a later one the next day. Tasks already created keep their cutoff.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.who: A seller whose merchant identity lets trade (`may_sell`), for its own merchant record only.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.field.cutof: A whole number from 0 to 23, sent as a JSON number or as a string of one or two digits.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.case.set: The hour is set. Tasks created from now on use it.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.case.notTra: Identity does not let this merchant trade, for example because it is suspended, so its store's settings cannot change. Its existing work can still be packed and shipped.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.case.notYou: The `id` is not the caller's own merchant record. Read it from `GET /api/v1/warehouse/merchants/me`.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.case.unread: The `id` in the path is not a whole number from 1 written in ASCII digits, so it names no merchant. An `id` in digits that is not the caller's is answered `403` instead. Checked after identity's answer about the caller.
rest.warehouse.setCutoffHour.case.invali: `cutoff_hour` is missing or blank (`cutoff_hour is required`), is not one or two digits (`cutoff_hour must be a whole number of hours`), or is above 23 (`cutoff_hour must be between 0 and 23`).
rest.warehouse.replaceCutoffHour.summary: The same action as `PATCH /api/v1/warehouse/merchants/{id}`, reached with `PUT`: the same fields, rules and answers.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.summary: Creates a storage bin, or updates the zone and shelf level of the bin that already has that code.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked. Every call an admin makes is recorded with the admin's account and its outcome.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.field.binCode: The bin's code: a string, not blank, at most 64 characters. Unique in the warehouse and compared exactly, case included.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.field.zone: The bin's zone: a string of at most 64 characters. Required when the bin is new; for a bin that exists, a missing or blank value leaves its zone as it is.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.field.shelfLeve: The bin's shelf level: a JSON integer, or a string of digits, from 0 to `2147483647`. A new bin sent without one gets `1`; for a bin that exists, a missing or empty value leaves its level as it is.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.case.updated: A bin with this code existed. The `zone` and `shelf_level` sent were applied, and the bin is answered.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.case.created: The bin was created. Goods can now be booked into it by its `bin_code`.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.case.notAString: `bin_code` or `zone` is sent as another JSON type than a string, or holds a NUL character. The message names the first such field: `bin_code must be a string`, `zone must not contain a NUL character`, and so on. Nothing was saved.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.case.invalidShe: `shelf_level` is given but is not a whole number from 0 to `2147483647` in digits: a negative number, a fraction, `true`, or a string such as `3a`. Nothing was saved.
rest.warehouse.upsertBin.case.invalid: The bin cannot be saved: `bin_code` is blank, a new bin has no `zone`, or a value is longer than 64 characters (`Bin code is too long (maximum is 64 characters)`). `error` joins every message, as shown.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.summary: Books goods into a bin for a merchant: adds `quantity` units to that SKU's stock in that bin. A merchant's `idempotency_key` books once; the same request sent again replays the first answer.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity must know `merchant_principal_id` as a merchant, and is asked unless the request replays an earlier receipt. Every call an admin makes is recorded with the admin's account and its outcome.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.binCod: The `bin_code` of an existing bin, created with `POST /api/v1/warehouse/bins`: a string of at most 64 characters.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.sku: The SKU: a string, not blank, at most 128 characters. A bin holds one stock row per SKU, owned by one merchant.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.quanti: The units received: a JSON integer, or a string of digits, from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.idempo: A string of at most 255 characters, sent in the body: this endpoint reads no `Idempotency-Key` header. Keys are per merchant. The same key with the same `bin_code`, `sku` and `quantity` replays the first receipt; with any of them different it is refused. Use a new key for each new delivery.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.mercha: The identity principal of the merchant who owns the goods, a UUID in any case; it is stored in lower case.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.field.note: Free text kept with the receipt, at most 1,000 characters.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.replaye: This merchant's key already booked this same receipt, so nothing was booked again. The first receipt is answered with `replayed: true`; `quantity_on_hand` is the bin's stock now, which may have changed since.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.booked: The goods were booked. `quantity_on_hand` is the units of this SKU now in this bin, reserved ones included.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.missing: `idempotency_key` or `merchant_principal_id` is missing or empty. A missing owner reads `merchant_principal_id is required: goods on a shelf belong to somebody`.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.notUuid: `merchant_principal_id` is a string, but not a UUID.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.keyConf: This merchant already used the key for a different receipt: another bin, SKU or quantity. Nothing was booked; send a new receipt with a new key.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.wrongOw: This SKU's stock in this bin belongs to another merchant. Nothing was booked; use another bin.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.notAStr: One of `idempotency_key`, `merchant_principal_id`, `bin_code`, `sku` and `note` is sent as another JSON type than a string (a number, `true`, a list, an object) or holds a NUL character. `error` is `INVALID_` followed by the field's name in capitals (`INVALID_MERCHANT_PRINCIPAL_ID` for the owner), and `message` ends in `must be a string` or `must not contain a NUL character`. The first such field, in that order, is named. Nothing was booked.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.invalid: `quantity` is missing or is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`: `0`, a negative number, a fraction such as `2.9`, `true`, or a string other than digits, such as `12abc`. Nothing is rounded or cut short, and nothing was booked.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.keyTooL: `idempotency_key` is longer than 255 characters. Nothing was booked.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.invalid: `sku` is missing, blank, or longer than 128 characters.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.binCode: `bin_code` is longer than 64 characters, more than any bin's code.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.unknown: Identity knows no merchant with `merchant_principal_id`, so no goods can be booked for it.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.binNotF: No bin has this `bin_code`, a missing or empty one included. Create it first with `POST /api/v1/warehouse/bins`.
rest.warehouse.receiveStock.case.stockLi: The receipt would take this SKU's stock in the bin above `2147483647` units, the most the warehouse can count. Nothing was booked; book the rest into another bin.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.summary: Writes stock off or corrects a count: adds `quantity_delta` units, negative to remove, to one SKU's stock in one bin, with a reason. A merchant's `idempotency_key` adjusts once; the same request sent again replays the first answer.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked; the stock must already belong to `merchant_principal_id`. Every call an admin makes is recorded with the admin's account and its outcome.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.binCode: The `bin_code` of the bin holding the stock, a string of at most 64 characters.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.sku: The SKU whose stock in that bin changes; the bin must already hold stock of it.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.quantit: A JSON integer, or a string of digits with an optional sign, other than 0 and from `-2147483648` to `2147483647`: negative removes units, positive adds them. A removal may not leave fewer units than are reserved for orders.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.reason: One of `DAMAGE`, `SHRINKAGE`, `MISCOUNT`, `RETURN_TO_SUPPLIER` and `EXPIRY`, exactly as written.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.idempot: A string of at most 255 characters, sent in the body: this endpoint reads no `Idempotency-Key` header. Keys are per merchant. The same key with the same `bin_code`, `sku`, `quantity_delta` and `reason` replays the first adjustment; with any of them different it is refused.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.merchan: The identity principal of the merchant the stock belongs to, a UUID in any case.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.field.note: Free text kept with the adjustment, at most 1,000 characters.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.replayed: This merchant's key already made this same adjustment, so nothing changed again. `quantity_before` is from the first adjustment; `quantity_on_hand` and `reserved_quantity` are the bin's figures now.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.adjusted: The stock changed. `quantity_before` and `quantity_on_hand` are the units in the bin before and after; `reserved_quantity` is the part of them held for orders.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.missingF: `idempotency_key` or `merchant_principal_id` is missing or empty. A missing owner reads `merchant_principal_id is required: adjusting stock adjusts somebody's goods`.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.notUuid: `merchant_principal_id` is a string, but not a UUID.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.wouldCut: The change would leave fewer units than are reserved for orders. Nothing changed; `max_reduction` is the largest removal possible now.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.keyConfl: This merchant already used the key for a different adjustment: another bin, SKU, delta or reason. Nothing changed; send a new adjustment with a new key.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.wrongOwn: This SKU's stock in this bin belongs to another merchant. Nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.noOwner: The stock predates ownership and names no merchant. Book a receipt for it naming the merchant with `POST /api/v1/warehouse/stock_receipts`, which gives the stock its owner, then adjust.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.notAStri: One of `idempotency_key`, `merchant_principal_id`, `bin_code`, `sku`, `reason` and `note` is sent as another JSON type than a string (a number, `true`, a list, an object) or holds a NUL character. `error` is `INVALID_` followed by the field's name in capitals (`INVALID_MERCHANT_PRINCIPAL_ID` for the owner), and `message` ends in `must be a string` or `must not contain a NUL character`, as here. The first such field, in that order, is named. Nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.invalidD: `quantity_delta` is missing, `0`, or not a whole number from `-2147483648` to `2147483647`: a fraction, `true`, or a string other than an optional sign and digits. Nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.unknownR: `reason` is missing or not one of the five reasons.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.keyTooLo: `idempotency_key` is longer than 255 characters. Nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.binCodeT: `bin_code` is longer than 64 characters, more than any bin's code.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.binNotFo: No bin has this `bin_code`, a missing or empty one included.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.stockNot: The bin holds no stock of this SKU, so there is nothing to adjust.
rest.warehouse.adjustStock.case.stockLim: The change would take this SKU's stock in the bin above `2147483647` units, the most the warehouse can count. Nothing changed.
rest.warehouse.listBins.summary: Lists the bins in order of `bin_code`, each with how many SKUs it holds and its units, one page at a time.
rest.warehouse.listBins.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked. A read is not recorded as an admin action.
rest.warehouse.listBins.field.after: The `next_after` of the previous page: the list goes on with the bins whose code sorts after it. A string of 1 to 64 characters.
rest.warehouse.listBins.field.limit: Rows per page: a whole number from `1` to `100` written in digits; `50` when it is left out.
rest.warehouse.listBins.case.page: A page of bins. `sku_count` counts the SKUs with at least one unit in the bin, `quantity` adds the units of every SKU, and `reserved_quantity` is the part of them held for orders; an empty bin reads `0` for all three. `updated_at` is when the bin itself last changed, not its stock. `next_after` is the last code on the page while more bins follow.
rest.warehouse.listBins.case.lastPage: The last page: `next_after` is `null`, also when the page is exactly full, because warehouse reads one row beyond the limit to know.
rest.warehouse.listBins.case.invalidAfte: `after` is empty, longer than 64 characters, holds a NUL character, or is sent as a list or a map. Checked after the role; nothing was read.
rest.warehouse.listBins.case.invalidLimi: `limit` is not a whole number from `1` to `100` in digits: `0`, `101`, `1e2`, a sign, or a list.
rest.warehouse.listStock.summary: Lists the stock of each bin and SKU, one row per pair, in the order the rows were first booked, narrowed by SKU, bin or merchant.
rest.warehouse.listStock.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked. A read is not recorded as an admin action.
rest.warehouse.listStock.field.sku: Only this SKU, compared exactly, case included: a string of 1 to 128 characters.
rest.warehouse.listStock.field.binCode: Only this bin, by its `bin_code`, compared exactly: a string of 1 to 64 characters. A code that names no bin finds nothing; it is not an error.
rest.warehouse.listStock.field.merchantP: Only the goods of this merchant: its identity principal, a UUID in either case.
rest.warehouse.listStock.field.after: The `next_after_id` of the previous page: the list goes on with the rows after it.
rest.warehouse.listStock.field.limit: Rows per page: a whole number from `1` to `100` written in digits; `50` when it is left out.
rest.warehouse.listStock.case.page: A page of rows; the filters combine, and none lists the whole warehouse. A row stays at zero once its units are gone. `quantity` is on the shelf, `reserved_quantity` held for orders, and `available_quantity` the difference, never below zero: the most an adjustment may take away. `merchant_principal_id` is `null` on a row that names no owner. `next_after_id` is the last row's `id` while more rows follow, else `null`.
rest.warehouse.listStock.case.none: Nothing matches the filters, for example a `bin_code` that names no bin: an empty list, never `404`.
rest.warehouse.listStock.case.invalidTex: `sku` or `bin_code` is empty, longer than its limit, holds a NUL character, or is sent as a list or a map (`sku[]=…`). `error` names the parameter (`INVALID_SKU`, `INVALID_BIN_CODE`). Checked after the role; nothing was read.
rest.warehouse.listStock.case.invalidCur: `after` is not a record id in digits: `0`, `+5`, `12abc`.
rest.warehouse.listStock.case.invalidLim: `limit` is not a whole number from `1` to `100` in digits: `0`, `101`, `1e2`, a sign, or a list.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.summary: Lists the stock receipts, newest first, narrowed by SKU, bin or merchant.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked. A read is not recorded as an admin action.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.field.sku: Only this SKU, compared exactly, case included: a string of 1 to 128 characters.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.field.binCod: Only this bin, by its `bin_code`, compared exactly: a string of 1 to 64 characters. A code that names no bin finds nothing; it is not an error.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.field.mercha: Only the goods of this merchant: its identity principal, a UUID in either case.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.field.before: The `next_before_id` of the previous page; the page starts with the entry just older than it.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.field.limit: Rows per page: a whole number from `1` to `100` written in digits; `50` when it is left out.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.case.page: A page of receipts, each the units one delivery booked into one bin, with the admin who booked it in `received_by_principal_id`. `note` is `null` when none was given, and `merchant_principal_id` is `null` on a receipt that names no owner. The client's `idempotency_key` is not answered. `next_before_id` is the last receipt's `id` while older receipts follow, else `null`.
rest.warehouse.listReceipts.case.invalid: `sku` or `bin_code` is empty, longer than its limit, holds a NUL character, or is sent as a list or a map (`sku[]=…`). `error` names the parameter (`INVALID_SKU`, `INVALID_BIN_CODE`). Checked after the role; nothing was read.
`before` is not a record id in digits: `0`, `+5`, `12abc`.
`limit` is not a whole number from `1` to `100` in digits: `0`, `101`, `1e2`, a sign, or a list.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.summary: Lists the stock adjustments, newest first, narrowed by SKU, bin or merchant.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.who: Staff: a token whose role is `admin`, and only from Kinetix's staff network; elsewhere Kong refuses it, see Kong's answers. Identity is not asked. A read is not recorded as an admin action.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.field.sku: Only this SKU, compared exactly, case included: a string of 1 to 128 characters.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.field.bin: Only this bin, by its `bin_code`, compared exactly: a string of 1 to 64 characters. A code that names no bin finds nothing; it is not an error.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.field.mer: Only the goods of this merchant: its identity principal, a UUID in either case.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.field.bef: The `next_before_id` of the previous page; the page starts with the entry just older than it.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.field.lim: Rows per page: a whole number from `1` to `100` written in digits; `50` when it is left out.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.case.page: A page of adjustments, each with the change, the units in the bin before and after it, the `reason`, and the admin who made it in `adjusted_by_principal_id`. `note` is `null` when none was given. `next_before_id` is the last adjustment's `id` while older ones follow, else `null`.
rest.warehouse.listAdjustments.case.inva: `sku` or `bin_code` is empty, longer than its limit, holds a NUL character, or is sent as a list or a map (`sku[]=…`). `error` names the parameter (`INVALID_SKU`, `INVALID_BIN_CODE`). Checked after the role; nothing was read.
`before` is not a record id in digits: `0`, `+5`, `12abc`.
`limit` is not a whole number from `1` to `100` in digits: `0`, `101`, `1e2`, a sign, or a list.
